subtasks.title: SQLite facts for small web apps
subtasks.instructions: Find official or reputable sources (sqlite.org, well-known engineering blogs) on SQLite's features, limits, concurrency model, and suitability for small web apps. Quote each fact with its source.

subtasks.title: PostgreSQL facts for small web apps

s1.title: SQLite facts for small web apps
s1.reason: stopped: step limit reached (6 LLM calls)

findings.title: SQLite is a single-file, zero-config database
findings.detail: SQLite stores the entire database in a single cross-platform file, making it easy to install, deploy, and back up for small web apps.

evidence.quote: the resulting database is a single file that can be written to a USB memory stick or emailed to a colleague.

findings.title: SQLite works as a server-side data store
findings.detail: Developers report success using SQLite as the storage engine for application-specific web servers, often faster than a client/server SQL engine in that scenario.

evidence.quote: Developers report that SQLite is often faster than a client/server SQL database engine in this scenario.

findings.title: Concurrency is managed by the server, not SQLite
findings.detail: In the server-side pattern, the application serializes database requests, so SQLite's limited concurrent-write model is not a bottleneck for small apps.

evidence.quote: Database requests are serialized by the server, so concurrency is not an issue.

findings.title: Database sharding scales SQLite for many connections
findings.detail: Using a separate SQLite file per user/subdomain lets a server handle hundreds or thousands of simultaneous connections, each hitting its own file.

evidence.quote: the server might have a separate SQLite database for each user, so that the server can handle hundreds or thousands of simultaneous connections

findings.title: SQLite is easier to install and use than an enterprise RDBMS
findings.detail: For small apps, SQLite's main advantage over a client/server database is simpler installation and a self-contained file format.

evidence.quote: The advantage of SQLite is that it is easier to install and use and the resulting database is a single file

s2.title: PostgreSQL facts for small web apps

findings.title: PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source object-relational DB
findings.detail: Official site describes PostgreSQL as a powerful, open source object-relational database with nearly 40 years of development.

evidence.quote: PostgreSQL is a powerful, open source object-relational database system that uses and extends the SQL language combined with many features that safely store and scale the most complicated data workloads.

findings.title: ACID-compliant since 2001
findings.detail: PostgreSQL has been ACID-compliant since 2001, ensuring transactional integrity for web apps.

evidence.quote: PostgreSQL runs on all major operating systems , has been ACID -compliant since 2001, and has powerful add-ons such as the popular PostGIS geospatial database extender.

findings.title: MVCC concurrency model
findings.detail: PostgreSQL uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) for concurrent read/write operations without blocking.

findings.title: SQL:2023 Core conformance
findings.detail: As of v18 (Sept 2025), PostgreSQL conforms to at least 170 of 177 mandatory SQL:2023 Core features.

evidence.quote: As of the version 18 release in September 2025, PostgreSQL conforms to at least 170 of the 177 mandatory features for SQL:2023 Core conformance.

findings.title: Rich data types and extensibility
findings.detail: Supports JSON/JSONB, arrays, UUIDs, custom types, and procedural languages (Python, Perl, etc.) for flexible web app storage.

s2.summary: PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source, ACID-compliant object-relational database with MVCC concurrency, rich data types, and SQL:2023 conformance, making it suitable for small web apps needing reliability and extensibility.
s2.feedback: All quotes verified in the official postgresql.org/about page; findings are on-topic, accurate, and properly sourced.
